definition: Caffe (Convolutional Architecture for Fast Feature Embedding) is a deep learning framework, originally developed at University of California, Berkeley.
details: It is open source, under a BSD license. It is written in C++, with a Python interface.

explainer.lead: Caffe is an open-source framework for building deep-learning software. Originally developed at the University of California, Berkeley, it gives developers a C++ foundation with a Python interface.

tiers.eli5: Caffe is like a ready-made workshop for building computer programs that learn from examples. Instead of making every tool yourself, you can use its tools to put your learning program together. You can work with it using either C++ or Python.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can use Caffe as the deep-learning framework within a C++ codebase or access it through its Python interface. Its BSD-licensed open-source code makes the framework available for inspection and adaptation.
tiers.paperLevel: Caffe (Convolutional Architecture for Fast Feature Embedding) is an open-source deep-learning framework implemented in C++ and exposed through a Python interface. It originated at the University of California, Berkeley and is distributed under a BSD license.

explainer.example: A developer building an image classifier could use Caffe as its deep-learning framework, writing the surrounding application in C++ and using the Python interface when Python is more convenient.

usedIn.name: Deep-learning development
usedIn.detail: Provides a framework for building deep-learning projects.

usedIn.name: C++ software projects
usedIn.detail: Fits projects that want to work directly with Caffe's C++ implementation.

usedIn.name: Python-based workflows
usedIn.detail: Allows developers to interact with the framework through Python.

explainer.intuition: A deep-learning framework supplies the software foundation for a learning system, so developers do not have to construct every part themselves. Caffe provides that foundation in C++, while its Python interface offers another way to use it.
howItWorks: Start with a deep-learning task that needs a software framework.
Use Caffe's C++ implementation as the foundation.
Interact with it directly in C++ or through the Python interface.
Adapt the open-source code when a project requires changes.
explainer.whyItMatters: Caffe combines a C++ deep-learning framework with Python access, giving developers two ways to work with the same tool. Its BSD-licensed open-source availability also makes its code open to inspection and modification.
misconceptions: Caffe is a framework, not a single trained model or a dataset.
Its Python interface does not mean it is written in Python; the framework itself is written in C++.

diagram.caption: A project can use Caffe directly through C++ or reach the C++ framework through its Python interface.
